## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial packaging format and validation manifest

## Description

This epic defines the tutorial packaging format: the contract that makes a
tutorial a versioned, independently testable artifact, decoupled from
Dashboard releases. It specifies the tutorial package metadata, the pinned
image references a tutorial runs on, and the validation manifest used to test
a tutorial against a platform release, plus the validation mechanism that
executes that manifest. This is the shared interface that the Dashboard
tutorial gallery's launch mechanics consume and that every curated tutorial
is packaged with.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial package structure: metadata identifying the tutorial
  (title, journey, description), the pinned workbench images it runs on, and
  pointers to the tutorial payload (notebook or pipeline definition).
- Define the validation manifest schema: the machine-checkable statement of
  what a tutorial must satisfy against a given platform release, so tutorial
  testing runs without a Dashboard release.
- Define the versioning model for tutorial packages so tutorials can be
  updated and re-tested independently of Dashboard release cadence.
- Provide the validation mechanism that checks a packaged tutorial against
  its manifest and reports a deterministic pass/fail result.
- Produce a worked example package demonstrating the format end to end.
- Review the format with the teams that build the gallery and author the
  tutorials, and record their acceptance.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The format specification documents the package metadata fields, pinned
  image references, and validation manifest, such that a third party can
  package a tutorial without further guidance.
- A tutorial packaged per the format can be versioned and re-tested without
  a Dashboard release (a version bump of a tutorial package does not require
  any Dashboard change).
- The validation mechanism, run against the worked example package, produces
  a deterministic pass result; run against a deliberately broken package, it
  produces a deterministic fail result identifying the violated manifest
  entries.
- The specification is reviewed and accepted by the teams implementing the
  gallery and authoring the tutorials, with the acceptance recorded.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P1)** — tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images,
  validation manifest) defined so tutorials are versioned and testable
  independently of Dashboard releases. This epic covers HLR-3 in full.
  Note: this epic is scheduled at P0 (not the HLR's stated P1) because it is
  the shared contract that all P0 work in this strategy builds against —
  priority inheritance applies.

# Dashboard tutorial gallery and launch mechanics

## Description

This epic delivers the product-code half of the tutorial gallery: a curated
tutorial gallery surface in the Dashboard from which a user can launch a
tutorial into their own project with one click — opening a workbench
preloaded with the tutorial notebook, or importing the tutorial pipeline
into the project. The gallery reads tutorial packages conforming to the
tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest).

## Scope

- Add the tutorial gallery surface to the Dashboard: a browsable, curated
  listing of tutorial packages with their metadata (title, journey,
  description).
- Implement one-click launch for notebook tutorials: launching creates a
  workbench in the user's project running the tutorial's pinned image with
  the tutorial notebook loaded.
- Implement one-click launch for pipeline tutorials: launching imports the
  tutorial's pipeline definition into the user's project.
- Consume tutorial packages in the defined packaging format so the gallery's
  tutorial set can be updated independently of Dashboard releases.
- Verify launch behavior with a format-conformant tutorial package
  (including the packaging format's worked example) end to end in a clean
  project.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user can open the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard and see the curated
  tutorials with their metadata.
- Launching a notebook tutorial from the gallery opens a workbench in the
  user's project, running the tutorial's pinned image with the tutorial
  notebook loaded.
- Launching a pipeline tutorial from the gallery imports the pipeline into
  the user's project.
- The gallery's launch mechanics consume tutorial packages conforming to the
  defined packaging format: a format-conformant tutorial package (not
  hand-wired into the Dashboard) launches successfully end to end in a clean
  project.
- Launching a tutorial into a project does not affect other projects or
  other users' workbenches.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — the Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user
  can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the
  notebook, or importing the pipeline). This epic covers HLR-1 in full.

# Author five notebook-based getting-started tutorials

## Description

This epic authors the notebook-based portion of the curated getting-started
tutorial set: five tested tutorials covering the core notebook journeys —
first workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, and first
RAG app. Each tutorial is a substantive content artifact, packaged per the
tutorial packaging format so it is versioned and testable, and validated
against the current platform release.

## Scope

- Author the five notebook tutorials, one per journey:
  1. First workbench — creating a project and launching a first workbench.
  2. Data prep — loading and preparing data in a workbench.
  3. First training run — training a first model.
  4. First deployment — serving a first deployed model.
  5. First RAG app — building a first retrieval-augmented generation app.
- Package each tutorial per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest).
- Run each tutorial's validation manifest against the current release and
  fix content until it passes.
- Verify each tutorial can be launched into a clean project and followed to
  completion as written.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist covering the first workbench, data prep,
  first training run, first deployment, and first RAG app journeys.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the defined packaging format, with metadata,
  pinned images, and a validation manifest, and carries a package version.
- Each tutorial's validation manifest passes against the current platform
  release.
- Each tutorial, launched into a clean project, runs to completion as
  written — a user following it achieves the journey's stated outcome.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)** — six curated tutorials covering the core journeys, each
  tested against the current release. This epic covers the five
  notebook-journey tutorials; the first-pipeline tutorial is covered by the
  pipeline tutorial epic for the Data Science Pipelines component (different
  component and team, so a separate epic per the epic boundary rules).

# Document tutorial gallery usage and contribution process

## Description

This epic authors the user and contributor documentation for the tutorial
gallery: how to use the gallery (browsing and launching tutorials into a
project) and how to contribute a new tutorial (the packaging format a
contribution must follow and the validation it must pass). Documentation is
written after the implementation work so it describes what was actually
built.

## Scope

- Author the using-the-gallery documentation topic: what the gallery is,
  browsing the curated tutorials, and launching a tutorial into a project
  (notebook and pipeline tutorials).
- Author the contribution-process documentation topic: how a new tutorial is
  proposed, packaged per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest), and validated before curation. Per the
  strategy's out-of-scope list, this documents the process only — no
  submission tooling is built.
- Keep both topics aligned with the delivered gallery behavior, tutorial
  set, and packaging format.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation covering using the gallery exists and accurately describes
  browsing and launching tutorials into a project, for both notebook and
  pipeline tutorials.
- Documentation covering the contribution process for new tutorials exists
  and accurately describes the packaging format and validation a
  contribution must satisfy.
- Both topics are technically reviewed against the implemented gallery,
  tutorial set, and packaging format, with the review recorded.
- The documentation introduces no submission tooling (the contribution
  process is documented only, matching the strategy's out-of-scope list).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — documentation covers using the gallery and the
  contribution process for new tutorials. This epic covers HLR-4 in full.
  Note on priority: the docs-authoring priority exception derives this
  epic's priority from the strategy's `priority: Major` field → P1 (not the
  HLR's stated P2), and this epic does not push priority upstream to the
  implementations it depends on.

architecturally distinct work streams with different owners and review
processes — product code (Dashboard gallery and launch mechanics), substantive
content authoring (the six curated tutorials), and documentation — across four
components (Dashboard, Notebooks, Data Science Pipelines, Documentation).

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 12/13 (framework → consumer) | The gallery's launch mechanics build against the tutorial packaging format: they parse tutorial metadata and pinned images to open a workbench with the notebook or import the pipeline. - **E002 ∥ E003 ∥ E004** — the gallery, the notebook tutorials, and the

  have — HLR-3 exists precisely so tutorials are versioned and testable
  independently of Dashboard releases.
- No `konflux-onboarding`, `repo-onboarding`, or `license-validation` epics:
